member_targets: Decision criteria or strategies for selecting a station layout that maintains efficiency across unknown order mixes and sequences
The specific methods or tactics cooks employ to reconcile or trade off station layout demands when different order types call for incompatible arrangements.
The particular shifts in the mix or sequence of incoming orders that make an existing station layout inefficient enough to require reorganizing it during service.

The decision criteria or reasoning process cooks use to select one station layout when competing order types favor different arrangements (i.e., how trade-offs between layouts are resolved), which the passage does not specify.
A decision procedure or set of criteria for selecting a station layout that optimally trades off competing access efficiencies under uncertainty about the upcoming order mix and sequence.

The ways station setup and layout are varied to fit a particular menu and workflow sequence — i.e., the specific adaptations of ingredient portioning, tool arrangement, and item placement across differing menus and station types.

The decision criteria or method cooks use to choose a station arrangement when different order types imply conflicting optimal layouts (i.e., how the tradeoff is resolved), not merely a description of mise en place benefits.
The decision criteria or basis cooks use to rank menu items when choosing station layout priorities, given that layouts optimal for one order cluster are suboptimal for another.

focal_unknown_anchor: When the mix and sequence of orders are unknown in advance, choosing the layout that best balances those competing efficiencies remains a planning problem.
